# Episode Prep: Kapil Dabi — Agentic Commerce

## Guest Research Brief

Research came back well corroborated on the professional side; personal/icebreaker material is genuinely thin (confirmed, not a search failure). Lean on the career-arc detail below rather than inventing color.

**Professional Accomplishments**
- Current role: Americas Market Lead, Retail and Consumer (Global Industries and Solutions), Google Cloud, since roughly January 2024.
- Career path: Managing Director, Accenture, cloud/digital transformation (~2015-2017) → Partner/Principal and Americas Digital Leader for Consumer Products & Retail, EY (~2017-2021) → SVP, Digital Connected Commerce (Omnichannel), Signet Jewelers (~2021-2024) → Google Cloud (2024-present).
- MBA, Indian Institute of Management, Calcutta. 20+ years retail/consulting advisory experience.

**Notable Projects**
- Cites in Google Cloud content: a home improvement retailer's AI visual search tool driving nearly $16M in incremental annual revenue; a consumer electronics retailer cutting contact resolution time 30-90 seconds via AI assistants; 125,000+ store associates equipped with an AI assistant at a home improvement chain; a fast-food ordering agent with a 95% success rate.
- Discussed Google's Universal Commerce Protocol at a Shoptalk fringe event with BigCommerce and other partners.
- Featured speaker, Google Cloud Next 2025.
- Could not independently verify personal authorship of AP2 or A2A specifically — he represents these Google-wide protocols publicly but no source credits him as their architect.

**Personal/Background Details:** Thin. Confirmed only: Dallas-Fort Worth based, IIM Calcutta MBA. No verifiable hometown, family, or origin story.

**Speaking/Thought-Leadership History:** Shoptalk 2025, Google Cloud Next 2025, Cloud Realities podcast (Capgemini, Apr 2025), commercetools Elevate 2025, Retail & Consumer Goods Analytics Summit 2019 (as EY Partner), author of a Google Cloud Transform blog piece on agentic AI in retail.

**Interesting Non-Work Context:** No verifiable personal icebreaker fact surfaced. Best genuine opener: his path from consultant (Accenture, EY) to client-side retail operator (Signet Jewelers) to hyperscaler vendor (Google Cloud) — three vantage points on the same problem in about a decade.

## Episode Prep Sheet

**1. Metadata** — Working title: "Who Pays the Robot? Google's Bet on Agentic Commerce." 30 min, single guest. Hook: as AI agents start shopping and checking out on customers' behalf, Google is trying to write the rules first.

**2. Philosophy** — Tension between hype and infrastructure: agentic commerce isn't a future concept for Google, it's shipping protocol work now. Audience should reconsider whether this is a 12-month architecture decision, not a 5-year one.

**3. Research Frame (5 bullets)** — Google's protocol push (Universal Commerce Protocol, discussed at Shoptalk); a live multi-platform standards race (Google, OpenAI, Visa, Mastercard, PayPal, Stripe); retailers' open-vs-wall-off dilemma; unresolved liability questions when agents transact; Google's own cited case-study numbers giving concrete grounding.

**4. Guest Expertise Breakdown** — Core lens is operational/go-to-market (consulting → client-side retail → vendor path), not deep technical. Will go deep on retailer adoption friction and cited deployment numbers. Likely bias: favorable framing of Google's standards vs. competitors. Credibility signal: a retailer detail not already in Google's public blog content. Likely hedge: liability questions and direct standards-race comparisons.

**5. Show Flow** — 5 segments, ~4/6/6/6/5 min, opener built on the verified career-arc detail rather than invented personal color.

**6. Four Threads** — (1) Who controls the protocol controls the margin; (2) the retailer's dilemma — open the gates or guard them; (3) trust, liability, and the agent that buys the wrong thing; (4) what commerce looks like when the customer isn't a person browsing a page. Each with 2-3 open questions and listening notes (recognition cues, not scripted follow-ups).

**7. Forward-Looking Questions** — % of transactions agent-initiated in 18 months; a bet Google could be wrong about; first mover category; which current standard won't survive 3 years.

**8. Closing Questions** — most surprising customer reaction; a specific shocking number; 30-second CEO advice.

**9. Post-Episode Capture Framework** — strongest verbatim quote, pain point/buyer signal, credibility phrase, what to do differently — feeds `episode-campaign-brief` once recorded.

**10. Credibility/Depth Signal Phrases** — 7 pattern-matches (specific protocol name + limitation, oddly precise number, disagreement with consensus, real failed pilot, GA vs. roadmap distinction, named liability edge case, admitted gap in Google's own approach).
